root_cause.text: The function cxl_payload_from_user_allowed() in drivers/cxl/core/mbox.c accesses the user-supplied payload via pointer casts and dereferences (e.g., uuid_equal) without first validating that the payload size is large enough to contain the expected structure, allowing an undersized payload to cause an out-of-bounds read.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description and KASAN trace show a slab-out-of-bounds read in memcmp, called from uuid_equal in cxl_payload_from_user_allowed. The patch adds explicit size checks (e.g., `if (in_size < sizeof(uuid_t)) return false;`) before accessing the payload contents, confirming that the missing size validation was the root cause.

The patch adds explicit size checks (e.g., `if (in_size < sizeof(uuid_t)) return false;`) before accessing the payload contents, confirming that the missing size validation was the root cause.

candidates.rationale: Directly assigns user-supplied pointer to struct pointer without verifying payload size, enabling out-of-bounds read if payload is smaller than struct.
Dereferences a field from the user-supplied struct without checking that the payload contains the full struct, leading to OOB read.
Casts user payload pointer to uuid_t* without size validation, allowing OOB read if payload smaller than uuid_t.
Calls the validation function without providing the payload size, so the function cannot perform size checks.
Function signature does not accept a size parameter, making it impossible to validate payload size within the function.

vuln_statements.explanation: Directly casts the user-supplied payload pointer to a struct pointer without verifying the payload size, enabling an out-of-bounds read if the payload is smaller than the struct.
Casts the user payload pointer to a uuid_t pointer without size validation, allowing an out-of-bounds read if the payload is smaller than uuid_t.
Dereferences a field from the user-supplied struct without confirming that the payload contains the full struct, leading to an out-of-bounds read.
Function signature fails to include a size parameter, making it impossible for the function to validate that the payload is large enough before accessing its contents.
Calls the validation function without providing the payload size, so the function cannot perform necessary size checks to prevent out-of-bounds reads.

    immediate flag is set.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function cxl_payload_from_user_allowed() is introduced in this commit. It directly casts the user-provided payload pointer to a struct type (struct cxl_mbox_set_partition_info) without validating that the payload size is sufficient to contain the structure. This allows an undersized payload to cause an out-of-bounds read when accessing pi->flags. No size check is present, so the vulnerable construct exists and is not fixed.
